items.title: Coverage gap: 55 unconfigured employer boards, and the 2027 cohort is filtered out entirely
items.description:
## Problem

An audit of a recent new-grad job export against `config.yml` turned up two independent coverage gaps.

**Source data:** a 359-posting / 168-employer new-grad CSV export (`jobs.csv`, columns `company,title,location,has_remote,is_agency,published,expired,experience_level,experience_years,salary_min,salary_max,salary_currency,views,clicks,foo_url,apply_url`), covering postings published 2026-08-01 → 2026-08-12. Each row carries the employer's real `apply_url`, which identifies their ATS — that is what makes the export usable as a *sourcing* list. No job data from the export would be imported; the scraper still fetches everything itself.

### Gap 1 — employers we don't scrape

Normalizing all 168 employer names and diffing against `config.yml`:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Already configured | 20 |
| Not configured | 148 |
| …of those, running a board on a supported ATS (Greenhouse / Lever / Ashby / Workday) | **55** |
| …of those, on an ATS with no fetcher in this repo | 93 |

The 55 include employers that ought to be on this board already: **Jane Street**, **Point72**, **DRW**, **Nextdoor**, **PathAI**, **The Home Depot**, **GE Aerospace**, **The Walt Disney Company**, **RBC**, **Philips**, **Luma AI**, **Sunday Robotics**.

Worth flagging: `docs/removed-companies.md` currently records Jane Street under *"Not added — quant firms use custom careers sites or recruiter-only flows"*. That is no longer true — `boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/janestreet/jobs` returns 232 open reqs. Same for Point72.

### Gap 2 — the 2027 cohort is filtered out entirely

`filtering.new_grad_signals` lists cohort years up to `2026 start` / `2026`. Campus reqs open roughly 18 months ahead, so the **2027 cycle is live right now** and every one of these titles is dropped on the floor:

```
Software Engineer Graduate (AML-Engine-Orchestration) - 2027 Start
Research Engineer Graduate (Monetization Technology - Business Integrity) - 2027 Start
Large Language Model Training System Engineer Graduate (Applied Machine Learning) - 2027 Start
Backend Inference Runtime Engineer Graduate (AML Inference) - 2027 Start
ML Infra Engineer Graduate (Ads Infra) - 2027 Start
```

Two things are missing:

1. **The cohort year.** `2027` / `2027 start` are absent from `new_grad_signals` *and* from the hardcoded `strong_new_grad_signals` list in `filter_jobs()` (`scripts/update_jobs.py`) — the two lists have to move together each cycle.
2. **Bare `graduate`.** The config has `new graduate`, `graduate program`, and `university grad`, but not `graduate` on its own, so the `"<Role> Graduate (<Team>)"` title shape that ByteDance, TikTok, and similar campus programs use matches nothing.

Running the current filter over the export: **116 of 359 postings are rejected for having no new-grad signal**, and 38 of those rejections are legitimate 2027-cohort or `Graduate`-suffixed roles.

## Proposed fix

1. Add the 55 live-verified boards to `config.yml`, each probed before adding.
2. Add `2027 start`, `2027`, and `graduate` to `filtering.new_grad_signals`; mirror the cohort years into `strong_new_grad_signals`; add 2027 JobSpy search terms.
3. Keep interns excluded — 2027 *Summer* intern reqs must stay filtered out.
4. Add a regression test so a bulk config edit can't reintroduce duplicate slugs, a wrong-source URL, or a Workday CXS API URL where the careers URL belongs.
5. Log the sweep in `docs/removed-companies.md`, including the 93 employers deliberately left out and the ATS each one uses, so the next sweep doesn't re-litigate them.

## Out of scope

The remaining 93 employers need new ATS fetchers, not config entries. By volume: iCIMS (13 employers), Oracle Fusion/Taleo (8), Workable (6), SmartRecruiters (6), ADP (6), Paylocity (5), plus ~30 on fully custom career sites.

The single biggest gap is **ByteDance — 58 of the export's 359 postings**, all on `joinbytedance.com`, which exposes no public board API. TikTok's Workday tenant is already configured and covers TikTok-branded reqs only. iCIMS or SmartRecruiters would be the highest-yield fetcher to write next.

items.title: [Sponsors] How sponsorship works here — current sponsors, hard limits, and how to propose a README CTA placement
items.description:
**This is a standing, pinned issue. It is intentionally left open — please do not close it.** It is the single public place where sponsorship happens in the open: what we accept, what we refuse, what it costs us to run this, and how anyone can propose a placement.

If you just want to submit a proposal, skip to [How to propose a placement](#how-to-propose-a-placement).

---

## Why this repo takes sponsorship at all

This project is free, solo-maintained, and runs a scraper against 224+ company APIs **every 5 minutes, 24/7**. That has a real cost in infrastructure and in maintainer hours. There are three ways it stays alive: people who [sponsor the maintainer](https://github.com/sponsors/ambicuity), people who contribute fixes, and a small number of products that pay for a placement in this README.

We would rather be openly, boringly transparent about that third one than pretend it doesn't happen. **Every paid placement in this repository is labelled "Sponsored by …" in the README itself.** If you ever see a product promoted here without that label, that's a bug — please comment on this issue.

## Current sponsors

| Sponsor | What it is | Where it appears | Relationship |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[Tailr](https://www.tailr.uk)** | Rewrites your résumé per job posting and shows an ATS match score. Free 10/day, no card. | `README.md` sponsor section + a badge on the [job board](https://jobs.riteshrana.engineer/) | Sponsor. Disclosed: a sibling product cross-promoted by the maintainer, not an arm's-length ad buy. |
| **[Zapply](https://app.zapply.jobs)** | Chrome extension that autofills job applications, plus its own job board and application tracking. | `README.md` "Website & Autofill Extension" CTA only | Paid monthly CTA placement under a written agreement. Not affiliated with the maintainer. |

Sponsorship buys **README real estate and nothing else.**

## What sponsorship never buys

These are hard lines, not negotiating positions:

- **No influence over job data.** Listings, categories, rankings, sort order, and dedup behaviour are driven by [`config.yml`](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/main/config.yml) and the scraper. A sponsor cannot buy a listing, buy a better position in a table, or get a competitor removed. Paying us does not get your company's roles surfaced.
- **No reader tracking.** No pixels, no analytics scripts, no third-party JS, no data about who read what. A plain link with a `?ref=` query parameter is the absolute maximum, and it is visible in the Markdown for anyone to inspect.
- **No editorial control.** Sponsors do not review, approve, or veto anything outside their own CTA block — not the README copy around it, not issues, not PRs, not moderation.
- **No implied endorsement of a hiring outcome.** We will not host copy that promises a job, an interview, a referral, or a salary.

## What we will not accept, at any price

- Guaranteed-job, guaranteed-interview, or guaranteed-salary claims ("we place you at FAANG").
- Pay-to-apply schemes, or anything that charges a job seeker to *submit* an application.
- Résumé mills, fake-experience services, or anything that coaches applicants to misrepresent themselves.
- Visa/immigration "guarantees", or products that prey on international students' status anxiety.
- Unpaid-internship marketplaces and training programmes that bill students for the privilege of working.
- MLM, crypto/trading pitches, and anything aimed at extracting money from people who are, by definition, currently unemployed.
- Anything requiring a database, a frontend framework, or an external orchestrator to be added to this repo — the [architectural constraints](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) apply to sponsors too.

New grads are a vulnerable audience with time pressure and little leverage. Our bar for what we'll put in front of them is deliberately higher than our need for the money.

## Where placements are allowed to live

- **`README.md` — yes.** This is the default and, for paid CTAs, currently the only place.
- **The [live job board](https://jobs.riteshrana.engineer/) — ad-free by default.** The site carries no paid CTA. Tailr's badge there predates this policy and is disclosed above; we are not adding more.
- **Job listings, `jobs.json`, the RSS feed, commit messages, releases — never.** These are data, not inventory.

## How to propose a placement

1. Open a proposal with the **[🤝 Sponsorship / CTA Placement Proposal](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/issues/new?template=sponsor_placement.yml)** template. Fill it in honestly — the checkboxes at the bottom are the rules above restated, and proposals that tick them falsely get closed and stay closed.
2. Expect a reply in **1–2 weeks**. This is a spare-time project; sponsorship enquiries do not jump the queue ahead of bug fixes.
3. If it's a fit, we agree terms **in writing, off this issue** (copy, destination URL, assets, disclosure wording, duration, fee, removal notice).
4. The placement lands as a normal reviewed **pull request** with the assets committed to this repo. Nothing goes live by side channel, and we never hotlink your CDN.
5. It's live when that PR is merged and CI is green — not when terms are agreed.

**Do not post pricing you consider confidential, contract terms, invoices, or payment details in this public issue or in a proposal issue.** Email `contact@riteshrana.engineer` for that. Public issues get indexed by search engines, quoted in replies, and picked up by archives and scrapers, so deleting a comment later does not unpublish what it said.

## For readers, contributors, and forks

- **Spotted a sponsor behaving badly?** If a sponsored product misleads job seekers, charges for something it advertised as free, or spams users who click through, comment here or open a bug report. We will ask them to fix it, and we will remove the placement if they don't. A placement is rented, not owned.
- **Reviewing a sponsorship PR?** Check three things: the "Sponsored by …" disclosure is present and adjacent to the CTA, assets are committed in-repo rather than hotlinked, and nothing outside the CTA block changed.
- **Forking this repo?** Sponsor placements are *ours*, not part of the project's licence. Please strip the Tailr and Zapply blocks from your fork's README — the [MIT licence](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/main/LICENSE) covers the code, not a sponsor's marks, and their agreements do not extend to you.
- **Want to support the project without a placement?** [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/ambicuity), [Buy Me a Coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/ritesh.rana), a star, or — best of all — a PR.

---

*Maintained per [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md). Kept open on purpose as the permanent public record of how sponsorship works here.*

items.title: Raise mobile breakpoint to 1180px so tablets reflow too
items.description:
Follow-up to #346.

At the current **760px** breakpoint, portrait tablets and landscape tablets in the 761–1180px band (iPad portrait 768, iPad landscape 1080, iPad mini 1133) fall into desktop mode and get the 3-column terminal, which has a **1180px min-width** and therefore scrolls horizontally on those screens.

**Fix:** raise the breakpoint to the terminal's own min-width — reflow to single column whenever the viewport can't fit the 1180px desktop terminal. This eliminates the horizontal-scroll band entirely:

- `≤ 1180px` → single-column mobile reflow (phones + all tablets)
- `> 1180px` → desktop 3-column terminal (fits, no scroll)

One-line change: bump `MOBILE_MAX_PX` in `docs/terminal/use-viewport.jsx` (760 → 1180) and the matching `@media` in `index.html`; everything else derives from that constant.

items.title: Make the terminal site mobile-friendly (single-column reflow)
items.description:
## Problem

The live site (`docs/index.html` + `docs/terminal/*.jsx`) is a desktop-only Bloomberg-terminal-style dashboard. On phones it forces horizontal scrolling and is effectively unusable.

Blockers:
- `#root { min-width: 1180px }` forces a 1180px canvas on every viewport
- `body { overflow-x: auto }` — the layout is designed to scroll sideways
- Both tabs use fixed 3-column grids (`210px 1fr 460px` / `220px 1fr 460px`) + dense 8–9 column tabular rows
- No responsive logic exists (`@media` / `matchMedia` / breakpoints all absent)

## Goal

Single-column **reflow** below a 760px breakpoint, for **both** tabs (Hiring + Contributors). Desktop layout (≥760px) stays pixel-identical.

Because every component uses inline JS style objects (inline styles beat stylesheet rules), responsiveness is driven by a JS `matchMedia` hook (`useIsMobile`) that components branch on; only the `index.html` `<style>` block uses real `@media`.

## Plan

- New `docs/terminal/use-viewport.jsx` → `useIsMobile()` (`max-width: 760px`)
- `index.html`: relax `#root` min-width + `body` overflow on mobile via media queries; cache-bust `?v=17`
- `app.jsx`: TopBar wraps, tappable tabs, condensed meta; footer padding
- `dashboard.jsx`: filters drawer accordion, stats strip horizontal-scroll, table rows → cards, full-screen job detail with BACK, hide F-key hints
- `contributors.jsx`: same single-column treatment

## Testing

Playwright screenshots at 320/375/768/1024/1440; assert no horizontal overflow at mobile widths; verify drawer + full-screen detail + both tabs; confirm desktop 1440 unchanged.

items.description:
### Summary

The **NGJ terminal redesign** (`262d287d`) replaced the original vanilla-JS/CSS GitHub Pages site with the React (Babel-in-browser) UI under `docs/terminal/*.jsx`. The old entry files were left behind as orphans — `docs/index.html` now loads **only** `terminal/*`, and nothing else references them.

CodeRabbit flagged on #336 that repo cleanup should land in its own PR; this issue tracks that cleanup properly.

### Dead files to remove

Verified: not loaded by `docs/index.html`, and zero references from CI workflows, Lighthouse config, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, HTML `<link>`/`<script>`, or any active `terminal/*.jsx`.

| File | Size | Was |
|------|------|-----|
| `docs/app.js` | 43 KB | Old vanilla job-board logic |
| `docs/styles.css` | 52 KB | Old stylesheet (index.html now uses inline styles) |
| `docs/contributors.js` | 6.7 KB | Old contributors-page logic |
| `docs/ui.js` | 3.8 KB | Old mobile hamburger nav |
| `docs/site-metrics.js` | 2 KB | Old metrics widget (zero references) |

**Kept:** `docs/contributors.html` — now a deliberate redirect stub to `index.html#contributors` (serves old bookmarks). Not dead.

### Stale references to fix (docs point at deleted files)

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — directory tree + Code Style section reference `docs/app.js`, `docs/styles.css`, `docs/stats.js`
- `docs/adr/0002-github-pages-deployment.md` — names deleted files
- `docs/architecture.md` — describes frontend as "Vanilla JS" (now React via in-browser Babel)
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml` and `05_advanced_issue.yml` — example text references `docs/app.js`
- `tests/test_display_count_copy.py` — comment about removed files

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] 5 orphan files deleted
- [ ] All doc/template/test references updated to the current `docs/terminal/*.jsx` architecture
- [ ] `make test` green; `pre-commit run --all-files` green
- [ ] Live site (`docs/index.html`) unaffected — still loads `terminal/*` only

items.title: Feature Tailr as project sponsor (README + terminal site) + add a Support section
items.description:
## Summary

The project has a real sponsor — **[Tailr](https://www.tailr.uk)** — but it isn't credited anywhere. The README has no sponsor/support section, and the site only exposes the Buy Me a Coffee (☕ SPONSOR) button, which is the *inverse* relationship (visitors funding the maintainer).

This adds an honest sponsor credit for Tailr and formalizes the existing support channels.

## Scope

**Website (`docs/terminal/app.jsx`)**
- New `SponsoredBy` badge — `◆ SPONSORED BY [T] tailr` with an inline SVG of Tailr's white-T mark, in the top-bar meta cluster **immediately left of** the existing ☕ SPONSOR button (unchanged).
- Links to https://www.tailr.uk (new tab, `rel=noopener`).
- Bump the `?v=` cache-bust token in `docs/index.html` so Pages serves the update.

**README.md** (hand-edited, outside the auto-synced `<!-- COUNT:* -->` markers — CI-safe)
- `## 💛 Sponsored by Tailr` block near the top (wordmark + honest one-liner + link).
- `## 💖 Support This Project` section (GitHub Sponsors + Buy Me a Coffee), mirroring `.github/FUNDING.yml`.

**Assets**
- `docs/assets/tailr-mark.svg`, `docs/assets/tailr-wordmark.png`.

## Honesty constraints
- Tailr is the maintainer's sibling product; its positioning explicitly calls for cross-promotion via the New-Grad-Jobs projects, so the credit is intended and truthful.
- Generic tech-company logos are **not** used as "sponsors". A separate, honest "Companies Hiring" logo wall is deferred to a follow-up.

## Non-goals
- Companies-hiring logo wall (follow-up PR).
- No change to the ☕ SPONSOR button meaning, footer, scraper, or `jobs.json`.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Tailr badge visible left of SPONSOR on the site, links to tailr.uk
- [ ] README has Sponsored-by-Tailr + Support sections
- [ ] Full CI green (pytest, pre-commit, codeql, pages build)

items.description:
## Summary

A candidate batch of 23 data / research / analyst job rows was submitted for evaluation. Per the "only add if working" rule (see #316), each distinct company was probed against the ATS platforms the pipeline supports — Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, and Workday — and only companies with a **live, verified endpoint returning active jobs** should be added to `config.yml`.

## Candidate companies (23 rows → 22 distinct)

Civic Nation, CharterUP, Tata Consultancy Services, Third Bridge Group, Adelphi Research, MRM (×2), Instawork, Life Chiropractic College West, Ensemble Health Partners, UST, Precision Medicine Group, Langan Engineering & Environmental Services, C2Q Health Solutions, CoStar Group, New York University, Liberty University, Senior Helpers, Workday, Amrit Ocean Resort & Residences, DaVita Kidney Care, XiFin Inc., YAMMII LLC.

## Probe results

### ✅ Verified working — to be added (Greenhouse, live jobs)

| Company | Slug | Jobs |
|---------|------|-----:|
| CharterUP | `charterup` | 13 |
| Civic Nation | `civicnation` | 7 |
| Instawork | `instawork` | 54 |
| Precision Medicine Group | `precisionmedicinegroup` | 167 |
| Third Bridge (Group) | `thirdbridge` | 115 |

### Already present (skipped)

- **Workday** — the software company is already tracked under `apis.workday.companies`. (Row 19 "Sr Cloud Engineer / Workday" is a role *at* Workday.)

(Most use iCIMS/Taleo/Workday tenants not currently wired, or are JS-rendered career portals.)

A couple relevant deep links:

- New grad / junior roles: https://jobs.hanzilla.co/new-grad/
- Canada internships / co-ops: https://jobs.hanzilla.co/internships/

If you think it fits, would you consider adding a small “Canada-specific companion resources” or “Related resources” note somewhere in the README/docs? No worries if that is outside the scope of this repo.

Disclosure: I’m the builder of Hanzilla Jobs.

items.title: [ROADMAP] Help us expand job data — all suggestions welcome!
items.description:
## TL;DR

We want to dramatically expand the job data this project surfaces, and we need **your ideas**. Whether you have a small tweak, a wild idea, or a full proposal — drop it in the comments. **All suggestions are welcome and I will reply to every comment.**

---

## Why this roadmap?

New-Grad-Jobs is most useful when it captures the widest possible surface of legitimate new-grad opportunities. Today we scrape and curate from a known set of sources, but there's a long tail of companies, regions, and job types we're missing.

This issue is the central place to brainstorm **how we add more jobs** — sources, regions, scrapers, partnerships, automation, data quality, anything.

## What kind of suggestions are we looking for?

Pick whatever resonates — these are just prompts:

### Sources
- [ ] Specific ATS platforms we don't yet scrape (Workday tenants, Greenhouse boards, Lever, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, iCIMS, Taleo, Eightfold, Phenom, Jobvite, BrassRing, etc.)
- [ ] Specific companies whose new-grad pipelines we should track
- [ ] Regional job boards (EU, India, LATAM, MENA, APAC, Canada, UK, etc.)
- [ ] University career portals worth aggregating
- [ ] Government / public-sector hiring portals
- [ ] Startup-focused aggregators (YC, Wellfound, etc.)
- [ ] Diversity-focused or accessibility-focused boards

### Job categories
- [ ] Internship pipelines distinct from full-time
- [ ] PhD / research / quant-specific listings
- [ ] Hardware, semiconductor, robotics, aerospace
- [ ] Game industry
- [ ] Finance / trading / actuarial new-grad tracks
- [ ] Bio / pharma / healthcare new-grad roles
- [ ] Trades, ops, supply chain, manufacturing new-grad programs

### Data quality
- [ ] How should we detect & dedupe reposted listings?
- [ ] How should we classify \"new grad\" vs \"junior\" vs \"intern\" more accurately?
- [ ] Should we surface salary data when available? From which sources?
- [ ] Should we flag visa sponsorship / remote / hybrid more explicitly?
- [ ] How should we handle stale postings (last-seen vs first-seen)?
- [ ] What metadata is most useful to filter on?

### Infrastructure & automation
- [ ] Scraper frameworks or libraries worth adopting
- [ ] Anti-bot / rate-limit strategies that respect ToS
- [ ] Workflow scheduling improvements (cron, GitHub Actions, queues)
- [ ] LLM-assisted parsing for unstructured careers pages
- [ ] Storage / dedup / canonicalization approaches
- [ ] Notification channels (RSS, Discord, Slack, email digest)

### Community & contribution
- [ ] How can we make it easier for contributors to add a new company in one PR?
- [ ] Should we publish a contribution template specifically for \"add a company\"?
- [ ] Would a structured YAML/JSON registry of companies + ATS endpoints help?
- [ ] Mentorship for first-time contributors who want to add a scraper

## How to suggest

Just comment below. Any format works:

- **A single company:** \"Please add `<Company>` — their careers page is `<URL>`\"
- **A source idea:** \"There's an ATS called `<X>` used by these companies: …\"
- **A feature idea:** \"It would be great if listings showed `<field>`\"
- **A full proposal:** longer-form design ideas, link to a gist or doc
- **A pain point:** \"As a job seeker, I wish this repo did `<X>`\"

You don't need to know how to scrape, write Python, or anything technical. **Ideas count just as much as code.**

## Commitment

- I'll **reply to every comment on this thread.**
- Concrete, actionable suggestions will be moved into their own tracking issues and linked back here.
- Larger themes will become milestones on the roadmap.
- Credit will go to the suggester in the resulting PR / issue / changelog.

## Ground rules

- Be respectful — this is a community space.
- Don't post anything that violates a source's Terms of Service or robots.txt; we want sustainable, ethical aggregation.
- Don't post personal data, recruiter contacts, or anything that could harm a company or candidate.
- Prefer one idea per comment when possible — it makes follow-up easier.

---

**Thanks in advance — every suggestion helps a new grad find their first job.**

items.title: [Feature]: add publish-time URL safety validation for jobs artifact output
items.description:
### Problem
The pipeline validates schema/contracts but does not enforce a strict publish-time URL safety gate before writing `docs/jobs.json`. Unsafe or malformed links (non-http schemes, localhost/private-network targets, invalid hosts) could be published into public artifacts.

### Proposed Solution
Add publish-time URL safety validation before artifact write/finalization:
- allow only `http`/`https`
- reject localhost/private IP ranges/metadata endpoints/malformed hosts
- surface blocked-count telemetry in health output
- optionally fail fast or mark degraded when violations exceed a threshold

### Alternatives Considered
- Rely on liveness checks only (too late: unsafe links may already be published).
- Manual cleanup through issue reports (reactive and inconsistent).

### 🏗️ Which area does this affect?
🤖 Core scraper (scripts/update_jobs.py)

### Constraints Check
- [x] This does NOT require an external database (PostgreSQL, Redis, SQLite, etc.)
- [x] This does NOT require a frontend framework (React, Vue, Next.js, Tailwind)
- [x] This does NOT require an external orchestrator (Airflow, Celery, etc.)

items.title: [Feature]: add automated duplicate-issue guardrail for triage quality
items.description:
### Problem
Issue backlog quality degrades when near-duplicate issues are opened (for example, repeated or reintroduced issue topics). This increases maintainer triage overhead and fragments context.

### Proposed Solution
Add a lightweight duplicate-detection guardrail in issue triage:
- on issue open/edit, compare against recent open + closed issue titles/bodies
- if similarity is high, auto-comment candidate duplicates and add a `possible-duplicate` label
- keep final decision manual (no auto-close)

This should preserve discussion quality while remaining maintainer-friendly.

### Alternatives Considered
Manual duplicate checks only.
This works at small scale but does not scale with automation-generated and community issue volume.

### 🏗️ Which area does this affect?
🔁 GitHub Actions / CI-CD (.github/workflows/)

### Constraints Check
- [x] This does NOT require an external database (PostgreSQL, Redis, SQLite, etc.)
- [x] This does NOT require a frontend framework (React, Vue, Next.js, Tailwind)
- [x] This does NOT require an external orchestrator (Airflow, Celery, etc.)

## Welcome to New Grad Jobs! 🎓

This template creates a **Good First Issue** — a small, guided task that helps new
contributors learn the codebase and contribution workflow.

**Good First Issues are pre-approved by the maintainer.** A contributor can claim it
immediately by commenting `/assign`.

---

### 🆕 Newcomer Friendly

This is a **Good First Issue** — a guided, well-scoped task designed for contributors
who are new to this repository.

#### What you'll do
- ✅ Read a small part of the codebase
- ✅ Make a focused, well-defined change
- ✅ Write or extend a test
- ✅ Submit and merge a pull request

#### Support
The maintainer actively monitors Good First Issues and will respond to questions
within 24–48 hours.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This issue does not require prior scraping or API experience.**
>
> - Basic Python and Git are sufficient
> - You must be assigned before starting — comment `/assign` to claim this issue
> - Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
>   before opening a PR

> [!NOTE]
> ⏱️ **Typical time to complete:** 30–90 minutes (once local setup is done)
> 🧩 **Difficulty:** Small, well-contained change
> 🎓 **Best for:** First-time contributors

**🏁 When this issue is complete, you will have:**
- ✅ A merged PR in a real open-source project
- ✅ Your name in the [Contributors Hall of Fame](https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/blob/main/CONTRIBUTORS.md)
- ✅ Confidence to take on larger issues next

> [!IMPORTANT]
> #### 📋 What makes a Good First Issue in this repo?
>
> **Often a good fit:**
> - Adding a missing company to `config.yml` (Greenhouse, Lever endpoint)
> - Fixing a keyword in `categorize_job()` or `get_company_tier()`
> - Correcting a typo or broken link in documentation
> - Adding a test case for an existing, already-working function
> - Small CSS/HTML improvements to `docs/`
>
> **Not a good fit for GFI:**
> - Changes to `filter_jobs()`, `deduplicate_jobs()`, or date parsing
> - New scraping source integrations (Workday, Google Careers)
> - Architectural changes to `update_jobs.py`
>
> Those belong in **Beginner**, **Intermediate**, or **Advanced** issues.

### 👾 Task Description

The `Validate config.yml structure` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` reads company counts from outdated key paths:

- Current code reads `config.get("greenhouse", {})` and `config.get("lever", {})`
- Actual schema stores these under `config["apis"]["greenhouse"]` and `config["apis"]["lever"]`

Because of this mismatch, the workflow prints incorrect counts and does not validate the nested schema as intended.

Please update the inline validation script to match the current config structure.

Suggested scope:
- Ensure required top-level keys include `filtering`, `apis`, and `readme`
- Read company lists from `config["apis"]["greenhouse"]["companies"]` and `config["apis"]["lever"]["companies"]`
- Keep behavior simple and non-breaking: fail only on true schema problems
- Keep output logs clear for contributors debugging CI

**Area touched:**
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CI validation step reads Greenhouse/Lever company counts from `config["apis"]`
- [ ] Required key checks include `apis`
- [ ] Validation output reflects real company counts from current schema
- [ ] Existing tests still pass (`make test`)
- [ ] PR is linked to this issue with `Fixes #<number>`
- [ ] PR title follows Conventional Commits format
